1.2  RECOMMENDED STRUCTURE: [TO BE CONFIRMED WITH COUNSEL]

   BASELINE RECOMMENDATION (absent specific deal facts): Reverse Triangular Merger
   with a §338(h)(10) election available as a negotiated fallback.

   Rationale:
   (a) Preserves Target's regulatory licenses and key contracts without
       requiring third-party consents that an asset purchase would trigger.
   (b) Sellers receive capital gain treatment on stock consideration.
   (c) Rollover equity mechanics fit cleanly into the surviving-entity
       capital structure post-merger.
   (d) Earnout payments can be structured as additional merger consideration
       under the merger agreement rather than as separate compensation,
       preserving capital gain characterization for sellers (subject to §483
       / §1274 OID analysis if deferred beyond one year).

2.1  §338(h)(10) ELECTION  [Available: S-Corp Target or Target in consolidated group]

   • Joint election by Buyer and selling shareholders (or S-Corp shareholders).
   • Treats stock sale as deemed asset sale for federal income tax purposes.
   • Buyer obtains stepped-up basis in Target assets (including §197 intangibles).
   • Sellers recognize gain as if Target sold assets; single level of tax for S-Corp.
   • Filing deadline: 8.5 months after close (Form 8023).
   • Price allocation: governed by §1060 / Reg. §1.338-6; Residual Method
     (Class I through Class VII); Buyer and Seller bound by consistent reporting.
   • Purchase Price Allocation (PPA) schedule must be agreed and attached
     to Definitive Agreement as Exhibit [__].

2.2  §336(e) ELECTION  [Available: C-Corp Target, 80%+ stock purchased by non-corporate buyer]

   • Unilateral election by Target (or consolidated group parent).
   • Achieves asset-sale tax treatment without buyer cooperation.
   • Consider when Buyer refuses §338(h)(10) joint election.
   • Allocation rules parallel §338 but election is made on Target's return.

2.3  §754 ELECTION  [If Target is a Partnership / LLC taxed as partnership]

   • Triggers §743(b) basis adjustment for transferee partners.
   • Buyer's share of inside basis stepped up to reflect purchase price.
   • Irrevocable (unless IRS permission obtained to revoke); consider impact
     on future transfers.
   • If Target LLC is disregarded, treat as asset purchase; §754 n/a.

2.4  INSTALLMENT SALE ELECTION  [§453 — applicable to earnout / seller note]

   • Sellers may elect installment reporting for gain recognized over time.
   • Available for capital gain portions of purchase price paid in future years.
   • NOT available for: inventory, dealer property, or amounts allocable to
     §1245 recapture (recognized in year of sale regardless).
   • Interest on deferred payments: §483 / §1274 OID rules impose minimum
     interest; test applicable federal rate (AFR) at closing.
   • Contingent payment rules (Reg. §15a.453-1(c)): if total selling price
     is contingent (e.g., earnout), seller must use one of three methods:
       (i)  Maximum selling price method;
       (ii) Fixed-period contingency method; or
       (iii) Open transaction (available only in rare cases per Rev. Rul. 58-402).

2.5  S-CORP BUILT-IN GAINS (BIG) EXPOSURE  [§1082 — if Target converted from C to S]

   • BIG tax applies to gains recognized within 5-year recognition period.
   • Coordinate closing date with end of BIG period if possible.
   • PPA should minimize gain allocated to assets with BIG taint.

3.2  TAX-FREE ROLLOVER STRUCTURING

   To achieve tax-deferred rollover treatment (Type B reorg or §721 contribution):

   Option A — Merger with Stock Consideration (Type A / Reverse Triangular Merger)
   • Sellers exchange Target stock for Buyer Parent stock (or NewCo equity).
   • Continuity of Interest (COI): ≥40% of total consideration must be equity
     (Rev. Proc. 77-37); maintain COI through closing (no pre-arrangement to
     dispose of equity received).
   • Boot: cash received is taxable; equity received is tax-deferred.
   • Reorganization Plan adopted prior to closing; documented in Merger Agreement.

   Option B — §721 Contribution (Partnership / LLC structure)
   • Sellers contribute Target equity to Rollover Entity in exchange for
     partnership interests.
   • Generally tax-free under §721 absent liabilities in excess of basis
     or disguised sale rules (§707(a)(2)(B)).
   • Disguised Sale Risk: if Buyer distributes cash to sellers within 2 years,
     presumed disguised sale; structure cash distribution timing carefully.
   • §704(c) layer created at contribution; allocations must track built-in gain.

4.2  EARNOUT TAX TREATMENT

   (a) Capital Gain Treatment (Preferred for Sellers):
       • Earnout structured as contingent purchase price under merger agreement.
       • Sellers report under open transaction or installment method (§453).
       • Each earnout payment taxable as capital gain to the extent it exceeds
         remaining tax basis; short-term if paid within 1 year of close.
       • OID: if earnout payments lack adequate stated interest (below AFR),
         imputed interest arises under §483 / §1274; portion re-characterized
         as ordinary income.

   (b) Ordinary Income Risk:
       • Earnout tied to continued employment of key sellers → IRS may
         re-characterize as compensation (Rev. Rul. 69-136; Coppola v. Comm'r).
       • Mitigation: de-link earnout from employment; ensure payments survive
         termination without cause; document as contingent M&A consideration.
       • If re-characterized: Buyer obtains deduction; Seller pays ordinary
         income rates + employment taxes.

   (c) Escrow Treatment:
       • Earnout held in escrow: not income to seller until release (Rev. Proc.
         2011-29 safe harbor; 70% of contingent consideration treated as
         allocation to Class VI/VII in PPA).
       • Indemnity escrow: not included in amount realized until released.
